rankingMethodology.fifthCompanyDecision: None admitted in this baseline. No fifth candidate received enough comparative underwriting to satisfy the same standard; this is not a rejection of other companies.

observations.title: GPU availability is only one part of useful compute
observations.sourceTitle: Why You Can't Just Rent 1,000 GPUs | Charles Frye (Modal)
observations.speaker: Charles Frye
observations.role: Modal; AI infrastructure practitioner, as identified by the episode
observations.summary: The official notes identify underutilization, peak demand and resource sharing as distinct problems. The full discussion still needs review.
observations.claim: Episode notes attribute a three-part compute-management framework to Frye; this seed does not verify his full reasoning.
observations.interpretation: Our hypothesis: software coordination can improve useful output without proportional growth in GPU purchases.
observations.countercase: Higher utilization may slow hardware additions for a fixed workload; it does not establish a public-company winner.
observations.nextTest: Review the 03:22–09:46 discussion and seek measured utilization or deployment evidence from an unrelated operator.
observations.location: Official chapters: 03:22 buying versus renting; 07:15 doing more with less; 09:46 conflict-of-interest question
observations.incentives: Modal sells infrastructure services that address these problems.
observations.verification: Official notes read; transcript and audio not reviewed.

observations.title: Customer demand is bursty and regional
observations.sourceTitle: Why AI Infrastructure must evolve for Agent Experience — Akshat Bubna, Modal CTO
observations.speaker: Akshat Bubna
observations.summary: Bubna describes elastic inference for custom models as Modal's largest use case. Customers serve multiple models across regions and encounter uneven traffic.
observations.claim: Bubna says autoscaling across models and regions is central to serving Modal's customers.
observations.interpretation: Our hypothesis: deployment and scheduling software may capture value beyond raw GPU rental; NVIDIA's system-level offering merits comparison.
observations.countercase: Modal's customer mix may differ from hyperscaler workloads, and software providers may retain the value themselves.
observations.nextTest: Find an unrelated operator's utilization, latency and cost results for comparable production workloads.
observations.location: 12:12–13:36, Elastic Inference, GPU Autoscaling, and Custom Models
observations.incentives: Modal benefits from demand for elastic inference services.
observations.verification: Speaker attribution verified in transcript; customer demand and economics not independently audited.

observations.title: An aggregator can shift capacity across infrastructure providers
observations.sourceTitle: Why AI Infrastructure must evolve for Agent Experience — Akshat Bubna, Modal CTO
observations.speaker: Akshat Bubna
observations.summary: Bubna says Modal pools capacity across 17 cloud providers without owning data centers. He describes reservation choices and reliability software as important to that model.
observations.claim: Modal's stated strategy separates its software layer from underlying rented capacity.
observations.interpretation: Our hypothesis: better aggregation may weaken differentiation among interchangeable GPU-rental providers, even as demand for compute grows.
observations.countercase: Reliable capacity, favorable power access and scarce regions can still differentiate providers.
observations.nextTest: Compare provider renewal terms, concentration and realized rental margins before inferring commoditization.
observations.location: 24:08–25:30, Seventeen Clouds and the Supercloud Strategy; 38:18–38:49, capacity planning
observations.incentives: Modal promotes its software and reliability layer.
observations.verification: Speaker attribution verified; provider count and commercial terms not independently audited.

observations.title: Prefill and decoding can need different hardware resources
observations.sourceTitle: NVIDIA's AI Engineers: Agent Inference at Planetary Scale and Speed of Light — Nader Khalil, Kyle Kranen
observations.speaker: Kyle Kranen
observations.role: NVIDIA Dynamo engineering leader and architect
observations.summary: Kranen explains that separating prefill and decoding can avoid scheduling interference. He describes their compute and memory demands as different and architecture-dependent.
observations.claim: Dynamo provides a way to allocate these inference phases to separate resource pools.
observations.interpretation: Our hypothesis: memory, interconnects and orchestration increasingly matter alongside arithmetic throughput; potential supplier benefits require deployment evidence.
observations.countercase: Disaggregation has transfer costs and will not improve every workload; supplier profit capture remains unproven.
observations.nextTest: Compare production cost at matched model quality and latency, including KV-transfer costs and network utilization.
observations.incentives: Kranen works on NVIDIA's inference platform.
observations.verification: Technical explanation read in transcript; no independent deployment benchmark evaluated here.

observations.title: The useful benchmark is the cost of a successful workflow
observations.sourceTitle: NVIDIA's AI Engineers: Agent Inference at Planetary Scale and Speed of Light — Nader Khalil, Kyle Kranen
observations.speaker: Kyle Kranen
observations.role: NVIDIA Dynamo engineering leader and architect
observations.summary: Kranen frames inference around quality, cost and latency. He emphasizes that serving decisions increasingly concern multi-step workflows.
observations.claim: The target configuration must satisfy the workflow's quality and latency requirements at acceptable cost.
observations.interpretation: Our research rule: compare cost per completed task, including retries and extra reasoning, before translating token growth into hardware demand.
observations.countercase: A useful evaluation framework alone does not show which vendor earns superior returns.
observations.nextTest: Collect matched-task completion, latency and total compute-cost measurements across competing serving stacks.
observations.incentives: NVIDIA benefits from presenting inference optimization as a systems problem.
observations.verification: Attribution verified; investment interpretation is ours.

observations.title: Supply-chain coordination may be part of NVIDIA's advantage
observations.sourceTitle: Jensen Huang – TPU competition, why we should sell chips to China, & Nvidia's supply chain moat
observations.speaker: Jensen Huang
observations.summary: Huang attributes supplier investment partly to NVIDIA's purchasing capacity and downstream demand. He also says component bottlenecks can ease while energy constraints persist.
observations.claim: Huang describes upstream commitments and coordination as an advantage, rather than claiming permanent scarcity in every component.
observations.interpretation: Our hypothesis: the durable advantage may be organizing supply and demand; a temporary bottleneck alone is insufficient for a long-term supplier thesis.
observations.countercase: This is an interested CEO's account; competitors also secure capacity, and commitments can amplify downside if demand disappoints.
observations.nextTest: Check filings and independent customer/supplier disclosures for commitments, concentration, delivery performance and utilization.
observations.incentives: NVIDIA's CEO is advocating its competitive position; this is not independent corroboration of its engineers.
observations.verification: Attribution verified in transcript; scale and durability of the advantage not independently established.

observations.title: Follow the customer's Ethernet scale-up work
observations.sourceTitle: OCP Defines New AI Scale Up Network Specification – ESUN
observations.speaker: Manoj Wadekar
observations.role: Meta AI Systems Technologist, as listed in the OCP catalog
observations.summary: The official OCP catalog lists a Meta technical session on an Ethernet scale-up specification. It provides video and slide links for further research.
observations.claim: Only the session's existence, title and speaker are verified here; no technical performance or deployment claim has been reviewed.
observations.interpretation: Our lead: customer-backed Ethernet work could affect scale-up networking competition and merits direct technical review.
observations.countercase: A specification or talk does not prove adoption, supplier selection, economics or market share.
observations.nextTest: Read the linked slides, review the recording, then identify published implementation and procurement evidence.
observations.location: 2026 EMEA catalog, AI Clusters section, ESUN session
observations.incentives: Meta has an interest in supplier flexibility and infrastructure cost; exact session claims remain unread.
observations.verification: Catalog only. Slides and recording not reviewed; publishedDate unknown, eventDate is summit start.

observations.title: Software can unlock hardware efficiency, but benchmarks need boundaries
observations.sourceTitle: GPU MODE Lecture 69 linked paper: Quartet — Native FP4 Training Can Be Optimal for Large Language Models
observations.speaker: Roberto L. Castro and Andrei Panferov, with coauthors
observations.role: ISTA researchers; named speakers for GPU MODE Lecture 69
observations.summary: Quartet reports FP4 efficiency gains using specialized Blackwell kernels. Its results are bounded by the tested models, formats and hardware.
observations.claim: The paper evaluates layers and Transformer blocks on RTX 5090 and leaves larger distributed execution for future work.
observations.interpretation: Our hypothesis: hardware/software co-design can extend useful output per chip; this historical result cannot establish current production economics.
observations.countercase: Kernel or block speedups do not equal end-to-end training gains, and techniques can transfer to competing hardware.
observations.nextTest: Seek independent distributed-training results and quality-matched total-cost comparisons on current data-center accelerators.
observations.location: Sections 4.4 GPU Kernel Support; 5 Experimental Setup and Speedup Results; 6 Discussion and Limitations
observations.incentives: Authors report funding that includes gifts from NVIDIA and Google.
observations.verification: Relevant v1 paper sections read; experiments not reproduced, lecture not watched, later versions not reviewed.

rankings.name: NVIDIA
rankings.confidence: High on business thesis; conditional on entry valuation
rankings.evidenceQuality: Strong issuer financial and technical evidence; independent customer evidence is mixed, as it should be.

leadership.name: Jensen Huang
leadership.assessment: Systems-level product integration and rapid platform execution are central to the thesis. Founder status alone is not an investment signal.

rankings.thesis: NVIDIA can compound through complete AI systems: accelerators, networking, memory orchestration and software that turn scarce power and hardware into useful work. Its ability to support changing workloads is a key advantage.
rankings.whyThisRank: Preferred to Broadcom because the operating results and breadth of deployed platform economics are more established, while its opportunity is less dependent on a handful of custom-chip programs. This is our business-thesis preference, not a verified current-price expected-return ranking.
rankings.strongestBearCase: Customers adopt custom accelerators while better utilization slows hardware purchases. NVIDIA helps finance demand that eventually proves less profitable than buyers expected, and exceptional margins normalize.
rankings.thesisKiller: Independent major customers repeatedly demonstrate materially lower total cost for their important workloads on alternatives, accompanied by sustained NVIDIA data-center share and margin deterioration across several quarters. A cyclical revenue slowdown alone is not sufficient.

reviews.summary: Started with four business theses: NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC and ASML. Customer evidence supports the shortlist; current-price return estimates remain open pending comparable earnings baselines. This is the first recorded ranking, so there is no prior score movement.

Changed the illustrative return horizon to ten years and added dated trailing P/E comparisons at the user's request. Existing per-year earnings-growth and terminal-multiple assumptions were retained. No thesis rank or confidence changed; this is a configuration update, not a new weekly investment review.

evidence.title: NVIDIA fiscal Q2 2027 results
evidence.summary: Quarterly revenue $96.221bn, data center $89.0bn, gross margin 75.0%; Q3 revenue guidance $108bn excluding China data center compute. Report also discloses financing partnerships, equity gains, rising receivables and investment balances. Guidance and management optimism are not verified future results.

evidence.title: NVIDIA Dynamo documentation
evidence.summary: Describes scheduling, request routing, disaggregated inference, KV-cache management and data movement across GPU fleets. Supports the existence of a systems/software strategy; does not independently establish its superiority or pricing power.

evidence.title: Anthropic: higher usage limits and a SpaceX compute deal
evidence.summary: Anthropic says it trains and runs Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs and NVIDIA GPUs. This independently confirms a multi-architecture deployment strategy; it is neither proof of GPU displacement nor a blanket endorsement of all suppliers.

evidence.title: Broadcom fiscal Q3 2026 results
evidence.summary: Revenue $29.591bn; AI semiconductor revenue $16.7bn, up 221% year on year; free cash flow $13.665bn. GAAP diluted EPS $2.68 versus adjusted $3.32. Hock Tan remains CEO. Risks include significant customers, manufacturing dependence and software acceptance.

evidence.title: Meta partners with Broadcom to co-develop custom AI silicon
evidence.summary: Meta describes a multi-generation MTIA program spanning design, packaging and Ethernet, with an initial commitment exceeding 1GW. It explicitly uses a portfolio approach to accelerators. The announcement supports a real customer program but does not disclose Broadcom's lifetime program profit.

evidence.title: Anthropic and Amazon expand compute collaboration
evidence.summary: Anthropic reports use of over one million Trainium2 chips and an agreement for up to 5GW of capacity. This establishes a meaningful alternative architecture. It does not establish that Broadcom receives the associated chip economics.

evidence.title: TSMC second quarter 2026 results and guidance
evidence.summary: Q2 revenue $40.20bn and gross margin 67.7%; Q3 revenue guidance $44.6–45.8bn and gross margin guidance 65–67%. Strong operating economics are observed; guidance remains conditional.

evidence.title: TSMC Q2 2026 earnings release PDF
evidence.summary: Reports diluted EPS of NT$27.25 or US$4.31 per ADR. Reported quarterly earnings should not be annualized mechanically as a normalized earning base.

evidence.title: TSMC Q2 2026 earnings call transcript
evidence.summary: Indexed company transcript excerpt says disposal and mark-to-market gains on Vanguard contributed NT$2.24 to Q2 EPS. Full PDF retrieval errored; retain excerpt only as an accounting verification lead, not full-transcript coverage.

evidence.title: ASML Q2 2026 results
evidence.summary: Q2 sales €9.326bn, gross margin 54.0% and basic EPS €7.59. ASML plans 30% capacity increases in low-NA EUV and immersion DUV for 2027, subject to execution; full-year sales guidance €43–45bn. Risks include order deferrals, customer utilization and export controls. Christophe Fouquet is CEO.

evidence.title: TSMC executives
evidence.summary: Identifies C.C. Wei as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.

evidence.title: AMD Instinct MI350X product specifications
evidence.summary: AMD's live MI350X specifications explicitly identify TSMC 3nm and 6nm fabrication. This corroborates actual dependence on TSMC by a competing AI accelerator designer, not merely TSMC's own market claims.

evidence.title: NVIDIA's Taiwan AI infrastructure supply chain
evidence.summary: NVIDIA names TSMC among its key wafer and chip partners as Vera Rubin production ramps. It corroborates TSMC's relationship to a leading AI platform but does not disclose TSMC's program-specific profit.

evidence.title: Intel Foundry and ASML accelerate readiness for High-NA EUV
evidence.summary: Intel reports High-NA use on select layers of a subset of Panther Lake products and says overlay, throughput and availability meet its expectations. Its count exceeding one million wafers combines certification, testing, R&D and production; it is not one million commercial production wafers. Co-announced with ASML, so count as one customer program, not neutral third-party testing.

evidence.title: Samsung expands ASML collaboration
evidence.summary: Samsung plans High-NA EUV for next-generation DRAM volume manufacturing by 2028 and participates in larger photomask development. This is a customer roadmap, not completed deployment, a booked order value or guaranteed supplier earnings.

evidence.title: TSMC and ASML large-format photomask initiative
evidence.summary: TSMC intends High-NA volume manufacturing for advanced nodes starting in 2030. The collaboration targets a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031 and larger-format system readiness by 2033. This supports long-term relevance while directly challenging assumptions of immediate broad adoption. It is distinct from current low-NA EUV demand.

evidence.title: Intel 2025 Form 10-K: manufacturing capacity and impairments
evidence.summary: Intel reported that some manufacturing capacity exceeded projected requirements and recorded $950m of manufacturing-asset impairment and accelerated depreciation in 2025. This is direct evidence that advanced manufacturers can overinvest. The filing does not identify those assets as ASML tools, and it does not prove a TSMC impairment or a current ASML order cancellation.

evidence.title: Intel Q2 2026 financial release
evidence.summary: Intel reports Intel 18A-P entering risk production and increased equipment, cleanroom and substrate investment. It confirms a competing technology effort and future supply response, not competitive yield parity or a demonstrated TSMC customer loss.

evidence.title: Broadcom September 2, 2026 Form 8-K with earnings exhibit
evidence.summary: The regulatory filing's earnings exhibit confirms $29.591bn quarterly revenue, $2.68 GAAP diluted EPS and $13.665bn free cash flow. It is the same underlying results as the press release and adds no independent evidence count.

limitations: The Information Bottleneck: official episode notes and chapters read, but no full transcript or audio reviewed. Its observation is a lead and cannot justify a conviction change.
OCP: official session catalog read; linked slides and recordings were not reviewed. The session is a research lead, not evidence of deployment or market share.
GPU MODE: Lecture 69's linked Quartet paper v1 was read in relevant sections. This is a May 2025 historical baseline; neither the lecture recording nor newer paper versions were reviewed.
Latent Space and Dwarkesh: full transcript pages were available and relevant passages were read. Speakers' operational claims are correctly attributed but not independently measured.
This seed contains no current valuation work, financial model revisions, procurement verification, complete HBM/packaging survey, or confidence-score changes.
